newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES LOWER IN MORE LIQUID MARKET.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES LOWER IN MORE LIQUID MARKET.

text.p: Zimbabwe money market rates were lower in a more liquid market on Friday, despite Thursday's shortage, dealers said.
"They're a little improved. The market was quiet short yesterday but it's much more comfortable today," one dealer said.
"We are starting to see it get more liquid and rates are lower compared to yesterday," another dealer said.
NCD bills redeemable after 30, 60 and 90 days were indicated at 18 to 18.5 percnt, while treasury bills were selling at 17.5 to 17.65 percent and being bought at 18.75 percent.
Call money was quoted at 16 to 18.5 percent in a market which closed short of Z$226 million on Thursday from a shortage of Z$82 million on Wednesday.
